title: Bianzhong
summary: The bianzhong is a set of bronze bells of different sizes hung in two tiers on a lacquered frame. Every bell is struck with a wooden mallet and rings its own note, so one player can play a whole melody.
howToPlay: Ten bells are lit: five large ones on the lower bar, five small on the upper bar.
Strike the bell a closing ring marks. It swings and rings out.
Bigger bells are lower. Let a deep note sound before the next one comes.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The bells are cast with a flattened, almond-shaped body, so each rings with a clear note and dies away quickly. Sets were hung and played at court.
credits: Tradition: the bianzhong of China; patterns written for this game
